solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Story about returning nobleman

indicators.note: returning tells us the short word for about is read backwards

parts.note: CA (circa) is the abbreviation for about
a count is a European nobleman

explanation.surface: A tale concerning a lord coming back home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' as the short Latin abbreviation is a crossword staple, and 'returning' flips it before the nobleman follows.
explanation.definitionFit: An account is a narrative report, so it is a synonym for a story.

clue.text: Rock stars holding note — they need skill

indicators.note: holding says the jumbled word contains the note
rock means to shake, so the letters of stars are disturbed

parts.note: TI is a note of the sol-fa scale

explanation.surface: Rock stars humming a note still need talent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rock' rearranges STARS into ARSTS, which holds TI.
explanation.definitionFit: Artists are practitioners whose work requires talent and craft.

clue.text: The man's caught in a questionable act, getting sleazier

indicators.note: caught in says the pronoun sits inside the word for a dodgy act

parts.note: a caper is a dodgy escapade
the man is he, with the 's standing for is

explanation.surface: A man caught in a dubious deed becomes more sordid.
explanation.definitionFit: Cheaper can mean more vulgar or tawdry, which is a synonym for sleazier.

clue.text: Golf club with no parking, say

indicators.note: with no says a letter is dropped

parts.note: a putter is a golf club

explanation.surface: A golf club that has no car park.
explanation.walkthrough: 'say' looks like 'for example', but it is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To utter is to speak, so it is a synonym for say.

clue.text: Management chaps with time to go after bonus

indicators.note: to go after places the chaps-and-time pieces behind the bonus

parts.note: a bonus or extra is a treat
chaps means men

explanation.surface: Managers and staff get time off after a bonus.
explanation.definitionFit: Treatment is the way something is handled, so it means management, as of an illness.

clue.text: Buy and sell vehicles

definitions.meaning: to deal or trade in goods, often illicitly
the cars and lorries moving along roads

explanation.surface: A dealer advertising that they trade in cars.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb the word means to trade; as a noun it is the flow of vehicles on a road.

clue.text: Following class daughter wrote on a keyboard

indicators.note: following says the daughter's letter comes after the class word

parts.note: a type is a class or kind

explanation.surface: After class, a daughter did her homework on a computer.
explanation.definitionFit: To type is to write using keys, as on a keyboard.

clue.text: A wharf with no end unsettled tunas — they'll swim deep

indicators.note: with no end says the last letter is removed

parts.note: a quay is a wharf

indicators.note: unsettled suggests the letters of tunas are disturbed

explanation.surface: Fish swimming off a jetty are restless in deep water.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with no end' cuts QUAY to QUA, and 'unsettled' rearranges TUNAS into NAUTS.
explanation.definitionFit: Aquanauts are underwater explorers who dive to great depths.

clue.text: On the house is a wild flower

parts.note: on the house means given free of charge

indicators.note: wild suggests the letters of is a are muddled

explanation.surface: A wild flower grows free beside the house.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wild' looks like it describes the flower, but it rearranges IS A into SIA.
explanation.definitionFit: Freesia is a fragrant flowering plant of the iris family.

clue.text: Camp bed that is supporting Queen

indicators.note: in a down clue supporting puts that is underneath the Queen

parts.note: a cot is a small bed
ER is Elizabeth Regina, the Queen
IE (id est) means that is

explanation.surface: A camp bed propped up by royalty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Camp' seems to describe the bed, but it is the noun for a faction.
explanation.definitionFit: A coterie is a select clique, like a camp or faction within a group.

clue.text: A thespian's initially found in that place

definitions.text: A thespian's initially found in that place

indicators.note: found in tells us the next pieces are placed inside the word for that place

parts.note: that place means there

indicators.note: initially picks out the opening letter of thespian's

explanation.surface: Where an actor is first to be discovered.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue also works as the definition: a playhouse is exactly where an actor is found.
explanation.definitionFit: A playhouse is exactly the place where an actor is found performing.

clue.text: Discreet priest with dirty religious books

parts.note: dirty, as in a smutty joke, means rude
NT is the New Testament, a set of religious books

explanation.surface: A careful cleric who keeps smutty scriptures.
explanation.definitionFit: Being prudent means being careful and wise, so it is a synonym for discreet.

clue.text: Split peas sorted and graded

indicators.note: sorted suggests the letters of peas are put into a new order

parts.note: graded means rated

explanation.surface: A grocer separates and grades split peas.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sorted' turns PEAS into SEPA.
explanation.definitionFit: Separated and split are synonyms meaning divided into parts.

clue.text: Busybody's a bloody snitch

definitions.meaning: a nosy person who pries into others' affairs
snitch is slang for the nose, so this is a punch on the nose that draws blood

explanation.surface: A meddler is a wretched informer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'snitch' looks like an informer, but here it is old slang for the nose.
explanation.definitionFit: A nosy prier is one sense; the other is old slang for a blow that leaves a bleeding nose.

clue.text: First hit of the ball from Spanish golfer carrying river

indicators.note: carrying means the golfer's name holds the river abbreviation inside it

parts.note: Seve Ballesteros was a famous Spanish golfer

explanation.surface: A Spanish golfer lugging a river as he tees off.
explanation.definitionFit: In tennis the opening stroke of each point is called a serve.

clue.text: Creatures great, creatures small, brought to earth with mysterious help

indicators.note: mysterious suggests the letters of help are jumbled

parts.note: ants are small creatures

explanation.surface: An echo of the hymn about all creatures great and small coming down to earth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mysterious' rearranges HELP into LEPH; the surface echoes the hymn 'All Things Bright and Beautiful'.
explanation.definitionFit: Elephants are among the largest land animals, so great creatures.

clue.text: Goad ounce that's wild with anger

indicators.note: wild suggests the letters of ounce are thrown into disorder

parts.note: anger means rage

explanation.surface: Provoking a big cat that is furious.
explanation.walkthrough: 'that's wild' rearranges OUNCE into ENCOU; an ounce is also a snow leopard, which helps the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: To goad is to urge or spur someone on, a synonym of the verb.

clue.text: Drink from plastic glass, we hear?

indicators.note: we hear says the phrase is to be heard, not read

parts.note: fake glass is a sham pane

explanation.surface: Drinking bubbly from a plastic cup.
explanation.walkthrough: SHAM PANE, spoken, gives the sparkling wine.
explanation.definitionFit: Champagne is a sparkling wine, a celebratory drink.

clue.text: One plays music to scare her, strangely lacking energy in one instance

indicators.note: strangely says the letters of the phrase are jumbled
lacking says a letter is removed from the jumbled pool

parts.note: E is the physics abbreviation for energy

explanation.surface: A musician wants to frighten a woman, oddly without vigour.
explanation.walkthrough: TO SCARE HER has two Es; 'in one instance' says only one is lost, and 'strangely' rearranges what remains.
explanation.definitionFit: A symphony ensemble is a single body that performs music together.

clue.text: Resisted work and assumed an attitude

parts.note: OP (opus) means a work
posed means struck an attitude

explanation.surface: Someone pushed back against work and struck a pose.
explanation.definitionFit: To have opposed something is to have fought against it, i.e. resisted.

clue.text: Bond with prisoner on floor

indicators.note: in a down clue on puts the prisoner on top of the other piece

parts.note: a con is a convict
to fuse is to bond together

explanation.surface: James Bond with a prisoner on the ground.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bond' looks like the spy, but it is the verb meaning to join.
explanation.definitionFit: To floor someone is to baffle them, which is to confuse.

clue.text: Awful loss? Hard blow

indicators.note: awful suggests the letters of loss are badly mangled

parts.note: H is the abbreviation for hard, as on pencils

explanation.surface: A dreadful defeat felt like a heavy punch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Awful' rearranges LOSS into SLOS.
explanation.definitionFit: Slosh is informal for a heavy punch, a synonym for a blow.

clue.text: Amigo and I at sea maintaining King's Japanese craft

indicators.note: maintaining says the jumbled letters hold the king inside
at sea means confused, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: R (rex) is the abbreviation for king

explanation.surface: A friend and I out sailing keep the king's Japanese boat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'at sea' rearranges AMIGO and I into OIGAMI, which keeps R inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Origami is the traditional Japanese art of paper folding.

clue.text: We hear how one might address Kelly's cleanliness

indicators.note: we hear says the greeting is to be heard aloud

parts.note: greeting the dancer Gene Kelly would be hi, Gene

explanation.surface: Discussing the dancer Kelly's tidiness.
explanation.walkthrough: Gene Kelly was the American star of Singin' in the Rain.
explanation.definitionFit: Hygiene is the practice of keeping clean, a synonym for cleanliness.

clue.text: Quantity of egg-flip in Christmas hamper

indicators.note: Quantity of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A little eggnog in a festive gift basket.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hamper' looks like the festive basket, but it is the verb meaning to hinder.
explanation.definitionFit: To pinch can mean to restrict or constrain, so it is a synonym for the verb hamper.

clue.text: Experience is hard — copying without something to write with

indicators.note: without is used in its old sense of outside, so the copying word goes around the pen

parts.note: copying means aping
a pen is a writing instrument

explanation.surface: Life is tough when you must copy work without a pen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' is used in its old sense of outside, not lacking, so the copying word wraps the writing tool.
explanation.definitionFit: A happening is an event someone goes through, which is an experience.

clue.text: From cloth I designed cloaks

indicators.note: from says the letters are taken out of the following words

explanation.surface: Garments I designed from cloth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cloaks' looks like garments, but it is the verb meaning conceals.
explanation.definitionFit: To hide something is to conceal it, as a cloak does.

clue.text: European cold in aeroplane — leave it abruptly?

indicators.note: in says the cold letter goes inside the aircraft word

parts.note: a jet is an aeroplane

explanation.surface: A chilly European on a plane wants to bail out.
explanation.definitionFit: A pilot ejecting is propelled out of the aircraft suddenly in an emergency.

clue.text: Heads back before new editor is knocked out

indicators.note: back says the slang word for heads is reversed

parts.note: nuts is slang for heads

explanation.surface: A new editor is floored when the bosses return.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns NUTS into STUN.
explanation.definitionFit: Being stunned means dazed or rendered unconscious, as if knocked out.

clue.text: Terribly enraged, Tommy might throw one

indicators.note: terribly suggests the letters of enraged are scrambled

explanation.surface: A furious soldier hurls something.
explanation.walkthrough: A Tommy is a British private soldier, who might lob a hand bomb.
explanation.definitionFit: A hand-thrown bomb is a standard weapon an infantry soldier might hurl.

clue.text: Doctor muddles, cutting top off bandages

indicators.note: cutting top off says the first letter of the synonym is removed

parts.note: muddles means messes

explanation.surface: A doctor makes a mess of applying dressings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cutting top off' removes M from MESSES to leave ESSES.
explanation.definitionFit: To dress a wound is to bandage it, so dresses is a synonym verb.

clue.text: Link hospital department with gripe on the radio

parts.note: ENT is the ear, nose and throat department

indicators.note: on the radio signals that a word is heard rather than read

parts.note: a gripe is a whine

explanation.surface: Someone calls in on air to complain about a hospital department.
explanation.walkthrough: WHINE said aloud sounds like WINE.
explanation.definitionFit: To entwine is to twist together, so it means to link.
